title: Rigveda 9.15: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.15: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.15 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 674r-674v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.15.1-7 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 674r
translation.original_text:
1e̱ṣa dhi̱yā yā̱ty aṇvyā̱ śūro̱ rathe̍bhir ā̱śubhi̍ḥ | gaccha̱nn indra̍sya niṣkṛ̱tam ||
2e̱ṣa pu̱rū dhi̍yāyate bṛha̱te de̱vatā̍taye | yatrā̱mṛtā̍sa̱ āsa̍te ||
3e̱ṣa hi̱to vi nī̍yate̱ 'ntaḥ śu̱bhrāva̍tā pa̱thā | yadī̍ tu̱ñjanti̱ bhūrṇa̍yaḥ ||
4e̱ṣa śṛṅgā̍ṇi̱ dodhu̍va̱c chiśī̍te yū̱thyo̱3̱̍ vṛṣā̍ | nṛ̱mṇā dadhā̍na̱ oja̍sā ||
5e̱ṣa ru̱kmibhi̍r īyate vā̱jī śu̱bhrebhi̍r a̱ṁśubhi̍ḥ | pati̱ḥ sindhū̍nā̱m bhava̍n ||
6e̱ṣa vasū̍ni pibda̱nā paru̍ṣā yayi̱vām̐ ati̍ | ava̱ śāde̍ṣu gacchati ||
7e̱tam mṛ̍janti̱ marjya̱m upa̱ droṇe̍ṣv ā̱yava̍ḥ | pra̱ca̱krā̱ṇam ma̱hīr iṣa̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1THROUGH the fine fingers, with the song, this Hero comes with rapid cars, Going to Indra's special place.
2In holy thought he ponders much for the great worship of the Gods. Where the Immortals have their seat.
3Like a good horse is he led out, when on the path that shines with light The mettled steeds exert their strength.
4He brandishes his horns on high, and whets them Bull who leads the herd, Doing with might heroic deeds.
5He moves, a vigorous Steed, adorned with beauteous rays of shining gold, Becoming Sovran of the streams.
6He, over places rough to pass, bringing rich treasures closely packed. Descends into the reservoirs.
7Men beautify him in the vats, him worthy to be beautified, Him who brings forth abundant food.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 674r (numbered 96r by the scribe) (OPenn image 674, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.14.6 ‹ati śritī tiraścatā gavyā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 674v (numbered 96v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.15.8 ‹iti tyam daśa kṣipaḥ›. Verses 9.15.1-7 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1eṣaḥ | dhiyā | yāti | aṇvyā | śūraḥ | rathebhiḥ | āśu-bhiḥ | gacchan | indrasya | niḥ-kṛtam
2eṣaḥ | puru | dhiyāyate | bṛhate | deva-tātaye | yatra | amṛtāsaḥ | āsate
3eṣaḥ | hitaḥ | vi | nīyate | antariti | śubhra-vatā | pathā | yadi | tuñjanti | bhūrṇayaḥ
4eṣaḥ | śṛṅgāṇi | dodhuvat | śiśīte | yūthyaḥ | vṛṣā | nṛmṇā | dadhānaḥ | ojasā
5eṣaḥ | rukmi-bhiḥ | īyate | vājī | śubhrebhiḥ | aṃśu-bhiḥ | patiḥ | sindhūnām | bhavan
6eṣaḥ | vasūni | pibdanā | paruṣā | yayi-vān | ati | ava | śādeṣu | gacchati
7etam | mṛjanti | marjyam | upa | droṇeṣu | āyavaḥ | pra-cakrāṇam | mahīḥ | iṣaḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 9.15.8 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 674v
translation.original_text: <sup>8</sup>e̱tam u̱ tyaṁ daśa̱ kṣipo̍ mṛ̱janti̍ sa̱pta dhī̱taya̍ḥ | svā̱yu̱dham ma̱dinta̍mam ||
translation.text: <sup>8</sup>Him, even him, the fingers ten and the seven songs make beautiful, Well-weaponed, best of gladdeners.
